title: Client telemetry sparklines — personal workpaper
content:
Context and goal:

This is a personal sketch for a tiny, lightweight telemetry artifact I want live at the client/proxy edge: compact per-request 'sparklines' (micro-timeseries) that travel with a request and surface important short-term signal for debugging and SLO tracing without pulling full traces or heavy spans. Intended to be embedded in request headers (or tight JSON envelope) so downstream services can emit, enrich, and consumers can render quick microcharts in the Console.

Why:
- Many customer support cases start with: "why did this request suddenly spike latency?"
- Full tracing is expensive and sometimes unavailable for customer environments (private deploys).
- We want a cheap, privacy-safe, compact summary that is interpretable by humans and machines and can be sampled and aggregated.

Design constraints:
- Max 256 bytes added to request on the wire for default mode.
- Human-interpretable ASCII-spark-like string for quick UI rendering, plus a compact binary/JSON payload for programmatic aggregation.
- No PII. Telemetry values only: timings, queue-length hints, batch-size hints, model-variant tag, sampling decision id.
- Should be append-only: each hop appends a single short cell. Idempotency: if header exists but hop cannot append (no budget), leave as-is.
- Backward compatible: systems that don't understand the header ignore it.

High-level representation (conceptual):
- header name: X-RW-Sparkline (or x-rw-spark for compact).
- payload: base64url( ascii-spark | '.' | compact-payload )
- ascii-spark: 6-12 char string e.g. "..__*^_" where each char maps to quantized latency bucket.
- compact-payload: short key:value pairs, max 64 bytes in compact mode.

ASCII spark encoding (proposal):
- map recent 6 samples (ms) to 6 characters. Window is last N micro-events within request lifecycle: ingress-queue, prewarm-delay, model-latency, post-processing, network-send, finalization.
- bucket thresholds configurable per deployment tier. Default buckets (ms): [0-5, 6-15, 16-40, 41-120, 121-400, 401+] -> chars: .,:;*^
- example mapping: [3,10,22,60,180,600] -> ".,:;*^" (human can glance and see rising trend).

Compact key/value payload (very compact syntax):
- format: v=1;id=abcd1234;sv=5;b=8;t=240;mv=redwood-3bq;sample=1
  - v: version of format
  - id: short request shard id (8-12 chars) for local aggregation
  - sv: sampling value (0-9) used by client sampler
  - b: observed batch size at model call
  - t: tail latency (ms, quantized to buckets 10ms)
  - mv: model variant label (short)
  - sample: binary sampled=1 for retention to trace store
- compress with base62 when embedding into header to reduce bytes.

Example header payload (human readable):
X-RW-Spark: eyJhc2NpIjoiLi46OioiLCJjb3JlIjoiIiwicHMiOiJ2PTE7aWQ9YWJjZDEyMzQ7c3Y9NStiPTg7dD0yNDA7bXY9cmVkd29vZC0zYnE7c2FtcGxlPTEifQ==
(above is base64url of JSON for debug mode).

Append semantics at a hop (pseudocode):
1) read header -> decode -> if invalid, create fresh spark object v=1,id=random8
2) collect local micro-samples: queue_ms, prewarm_ms, model_ms, post_ms, send_ms
3) quantize per-bucket and map to ASCII chars; keep only last 6 cells -> new_ascii = old_ascii + mapped_chars then truncate to last 12 chars
4) update compact kvs: increment b if observed, update t = max(t, model_ms), set mv if variant present (only first-hop should set?), preserve sample flag where set
5) re-encode -> write back header (only if resulting size <= configured budget)

Sampling strategy:
- default: 1% deterministic by id hash per tenant, with burst increases when error-rate > threshold (so ops can temporarily get more traces during incidents).
- mark 'sample=1' in compact payload to indicate collector should retain full trace/span in telemetry pipelines.

Consumer-facing Console ideas:
- UX surface: in request inspector show tiny ASCII sparkline in the header pane with hover mouse-over to show sampled kvs.
- search filter: sparkline pattern match: e.g., search for requests with '\^' (high tail spikes) in last N minutes.

Aggregation and storage:
- On ingest we want to keep counts of spark patterns per route/model/tenant. Aggregator will unpack ascii -> histogram of last-step buckets. Also keep average batch sizes and top-k model-variant counts. 
- For sampled=1 records, full trace id is emitted to trace-back store.

Privacy and security notes: 
- Never include user identifiers or prompt content. Only local shard id and quantized timings. 
- Enforce tenant-level opt-out; private deploy default may keep header off.

Failure modes and mitigation: 
- Header grows over multiple hops beyond budget: policy = drop oldest cells, mark truncated=true in payload.
- Corrupt header format: ignore and start new one (avoid leaking previous info).
- Adversarial injection: only accept trusted model_variant labels from whitelist where possible, and limit header TTL to a small number of hops.

Open questions and experimental knobs (todo list):
- Best base encoding: base62 vs base64url vs zlib+base64 for compact mode. Tradeoffs: CPU vs bytes saved.
- Character palette for ASCII-spark: explore UTF8 microglyphs (▁▂▃▅▆▇) — nicer visually but increases risk with proxies that don't like bytes. Stick to ascii for now.
- Which hop owns model_variant assignment? probably the service that actually invokes the inference runtime; propagate downstream as "mv=..." only if blank.
- Integration plan for Private deployments with strict header filtering: fallback to embedding in body metadata envelope when header blocked.
- A/B experiment: default 0.1% sampling and toggleable incident override endpoint for on-demand ramp to 10% for 30 minutes.

Quick API sketch for helper library (JS-ish pseudo):
function appendSpark(headerStr, samples, opts){
  // headerStr: incoming header string or null
  // samples: {queue,prewarm,model,post,send} in ms
  // opts: {budgetBytes:256, idProvider, modelVariant}
  // returns newHeaderStr or null if cannot append
}

Example tiny implementation note: quantize function:
- q(x): if x<=5 -> 0; if <=15 -> 1; if <=40 -> 2; if <=120 -> 3; if <=400 -> 4; else 5
- map to chars = ['.','',':',';','*','^'] (reserve second char for lower-mid maybe '-')

ASCII rendering in Console: monospaced font, color map to buckets: .->green, :->yellow, ^->red. Tooltip shows raw quantized numbers.

Small toy use-case flow (human story):
1) Customer hits API endpoint -> header created id=xx, ascii="......"
2) Request arrives at router -> appended char -> ".::..*" -> shows warmup then model spike
3) Service B sees high finalization time -> sets sample=1 -> telemetry collector pulls trace -> ops sees model variant 'redwood-3bq' and batch size=12 -> root cause: prewarm mispredict + high queue

Shipping path notes (personal):
- Prototype: add client lib to edge-runner + JS SDK to emit header (Q1 spike experiment).
- Collect terms: need new telemetry pipeline field (sparkline pattern) in metrics-index. Quick PR: obs/ingest schema v2.
- UI: add tiny sparklines column in request table, with a small modal to show kvs.

Back-of-envelope sizing:
- If 1% sampling on 1M requests/day -> 10k retained traces, fine.
- Non-sampled header size average ~80 bytes -> across 1M requests/day = 80MB/day additional traffic at edge (ok).

Notes to self: keep it optional and reversible. Start with prototype that only enables on non-production tenants; iterate on char palette after UX test.

End of scratchpaper.

Recent edits log:
- 2025-01-18: initial idea dump
- 2025-01-25: added compact kv syntax and sample flag
- 2025-02-02: clarified append semantics and failure handling
